# gps-digest

> Free web tool that turns GPS watch files (TCX, GPX, FIT) into a structured
> training file that ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude can actually analyze. A one-hour
> TCX file recorded at 1 Hz weighs about 1.7 MB, roughly 533,000 tokens, nearly
> 90% of it XML tags; the structured file for the same session is about 18 KB
> and 5,800 tokens. All processing runs in the browser: no file is uploaded to
> a server.

The site is published in seven languages with identical content: English,
French, Spanish, Portuguese, German, Simplified Chinese and Japanese. Each page
declares its translations with hreflang. The file exported for the AI follows
the language of the page.

## The tool

- [gps-digest, English](https://exemple.com/en/): drop TCX, GPX or FIT files, get a structured training file to paste into an AI.
- Other languages: [français](https://exemple.com/fr/), [español](https://exemple.com/es/), [português](https://exemple.com/pt/), [Deutsch](https://exemple.com/de/), [中文](https://exemple.com/zh/), [日本語](https://exemple.com/ja/)

## A year of context from one Strava archive

- Drop the full Strava account archive (strava.com/account, "Download your account" ZIP) as is. The archive is read in the browser in chunks, never loaded whole and never uploaded; photos and planned routes are skipped.
- The last 12 months are kept by default (choice from 3 months to the full history). Strava activity IDs grow over time, so reading stops once the period is passed.
- History file: the last 14 days are detailed session by session, older sessions take one line each, aerobic progression is aggregated by month. Measured on a real archive of 1,161 activities: 338 sessions over 12 months, about 30,000 tokens (about 12,500 tokens in summary-only mode), analyzed in about 20 seconds.

## What the tool computes on its own

- Heart rate sensor detection (chest strap or wrist optical sensor), inferred
  from the signal: cadence lock, plateaus, response lag. Read directly from
  the paired hardware when the FIT file provides it.
- Cardiac drift (aerobic decoupling, Pa:Hr or Pw:Hr) on the longest steady
  window of the session. Refused on interval sessions, where it would be
  meaningless, with the reason stated.
- Interval detection and execution analysis: rep consistency, pace or power
  fade, recovery times, heart rate recovery at 60 seconds.
- Best efforts, critical speed model (refused when D' is below 80 m, a sign of
  collinear efforts), race projections for 5K, 10K, half marathon and
  marathon, each with a range and a reliability level.
- Grade-adjusted pace (Minetti et al. 2002), Normalized Power, TSS.
- Session classification from the shape of the data, not from the sport
  label in the file.
- Pace is computed on moving time (Strava convention); Garmin Connect uses
  total duration. The exported file states which convention is used.

## Measured facts

- One-hour run, TCX at 1 Hz: 1.7 MB, about 533,000 tokens, nearly 90% XML tags.
- Same run as a structured file: about 18 KB, about 5,800 tokens.
- 15 MB of real training files: about 32,000 tokens as a structured file.
- Token estimates use 3.2 characters per token, the ratio observed on numeric
  CSV. Benchmark reproducible from the open source code:
  https://github.com/tpripri/gps-digest

## Articles

- [ChatGPT can analyze your running workouts. It just has to be able to read them first.](https://exemple.com/en/blog/analyze-running-workouts-with-ai/): why AI is a strong training partner, why a raw watch file breaks it (token limits, partial reading, "lost in the middle"), and why restructuring beats compressing. Markdown: https://exemple.com/en/blog/analyze-running-workouts-with-ai/index.html.md
- Same article in [French](https://exemple.com/fr/blog/analyser-ses-seances-de-course-avec-une-ia/), [Spanish](https://exemple.com/es/blog/analizar-entrenamientos-de-running-con-ia/), [Portuguese](https://exemple.com/pt/blog/analisar-treinos-de-corrida-com-ia/), [German](https://exemple.com/de/blog/lauftraining-mit-ki-analysieren/), [Chinese](https://exemple.com/zh/blog/ai-running-training-analysis/), [Japanese](https://exemple.com/ja/blog/ai-running-training-analysis/).
- [Turn ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Vibe into your running coach](https://exemple.com/en/blog/ai-running-coach/): athlete profile and coach rules to copy, setup in ChatGPT and Claude projects, Gemini Gems and Mistral Vibe projects, a weekly review routine, and the five traps of an AI coach. Covers how to get workouts to the AI: Strava's official MCP connector (launched June 1, 2026) requires a paid Strava subscription and only works with Claude; free file export (FIT, TCX, GPX) works with every assistant once compressed into a structured file. Markdown: https://exemple.com/en/blog/ai-running-coach/index.html.md
- Same article in [French](https://exemple.com/fr/blog/coach-running-ia/), [Spanish](https://exemple.com/es/blog/entrenador-running-ia/), [Portuguese](https://exemple.com/pt/blog/treinador-corrida-ia/), [German](https://exemple.com/de/blog/ki-lauftrainer/), [Chinese](https://exemple.com/zh/blog/ai-running-coach/), [Japanese](https://exemple.com/ja/blog/ai-running-coach/). Every translation of both articles has a Markdown version at the same URL followed by index.html.md.

## Export guides

How to get workout files out of each platform before giving them to an AI. The tool accepts FIT, TCX and GPX, plus Garmin ZIP exports and Strava .gz archives as is.

- [Export Garmin data (FIT) for ChatGPT](https://exemple.com/en/blog/export-garmin-data-for-chatgpt/): single activity from connect.garmin.com (gear icon, original file, delivered as a ZIP), USB copy from the GARMIN/Activity folder, full account export. The Garmin Connect mobile app exports no files. Markdown: https://exemple.com/en/blog/export-garmin-data-for-chatgpt/index.html.md. Also in [French](https://exemple.com/fr/blog/exporter-donnees-garmin-pour-chatgpt/), [Spanish](https://exemple.com/es/blog/exportar-datos-garmin-para-chatgpt/), [Portuguese](https://exemple.com/pt/blog/exportar-dados-garmin-para-chatgpt/), [German](https://exemple.com/de/blog/garmin-daten-fuer-chatgpt-exportieren/), [Chinese](https://exemple.com/zh/blog/garmin-export-ai/), [Japanese](https://exemple.com/ja/blog/garmin-export-chatgpt/).
- [Export Strava activities (GPX, FIT) for ChatGPT](https://exemple.com/en/blog/export-strava-data-for-chatgpt/): "…" menu on strava.com, original file or GPX (includes heart rate when recorded), bulk archive with .gz files in the activities folder. Export is website-only and free; Strava computes pace on moving time. Markdown: https://exemple.com/en/blog/export-strava-data-for-chatgpt/index.html.md. Also in [French](https://exemple.com/fr/blog/exporter-donnees-strava-pour-chatgpt/), [Spanish](https://exemple.com/es/blog/exportar-datos-strava-para-chatgpt/), [Portuguese](https://exemple.com/pt/blog/exportar-dados-strava-para-chatgpt/), [German](https://exemple.com/de/blog/strava-daten-fuer-chatgpt-exportieren/), [Chinese](https://exemple.com/zh/blog/strava-export-ai/), [Japanese](https://exemple.com/ja/blog/strava-export-chatgpt/).
- [Export Apple Watch workouts (GPX, FIT) for ChatGPT](https://exemple.com/en/blog/export-apple-watch-workouts-for-chatgpt/): no native per-workout export; use an export app (HealthFit: FIT/GPX/TCX, WorkoutGPX: GPX) or sync to Strava then export. The native Health export gives route GPX files without heart rate. Markdown: https://exemple.com/en/blog/export-apple-watch-workouts-for-chatgpt/index.html.md. Also in [French](https://exemple.com/fr/blog/exporter-seances-apple-watch-pour-chatgpt/), [Spanish](https://exemple.com/es/blog/exportar-entrenamientos-apple-watch-para-chatgpt/), [Portuguese](https://exemple.com/pt/blog/exportar-treinos-apple-watch-para-chatgpt/), [German](https://exemple.com/de/blog/apple-watch-workouts-fuer-chatgpt-exportieren/), [Chinese](https://exemple.com/zh/blog/apple-watch-export-ai/), [Japanese](https://exemple.com/ja/blog/apple-watch-export-chatgpt/).

## Privacy

- [Privacy](https://exemple.com/en/confidentialite): files are read and analyzed in the browser and never sent to a server. The only outgoing request is the optional weather lookup, which sends the route midpoint rounded to two decimals (about 1.1 km) and the date to Open-Meteo, never the start point. Start and finish of the track are trimmed by 250 m by default before any export.
